title: Nine St. George officers honored as TDS Hometown Heroes
summary: When a fire broke out at the Bella Vista Apartments in St. George, Utah, earlier this summer, nine local police… more...
body_markdown:
When a fire broke out at the Bella Vista Apartments in St. George, Utah, earlier this summer, nine local police officers didn’t hesitate to help.


Sgt. Burkeley Christian and Officers Kaison Kennedy, Michael Johnson, Austin Rogers, Helen Gallegos, Austin Faria, Omar Contreras, Greg Lovegren, and Andres Lepe were already on patrol when the June fire began. Arriving before fire crews, they went door-to-door through smoke and flames, helping residents escape the burning complex.


Their courage and quick response earned them recognition as TDS Hometown Heroes.


TDS honored the nine members of the St. George Police Department on the field at Greater Zion Stadium during the Utah Tech football game against Eastern Washington University on Saturday, Nov. 14.


“I am very proud of our officers and grateful they were able to save so many lives,” said St. George Chief of Police Kyle Whitehead. “Their bravery speaks to their character and embodies our mission to preserve life.”


The TDS Hometown Hero Award recognizes people and organizations that go above and beyond to make a difference in their communities. As a proud partner of Utah Tech athletics, TDS was grateful for the opportunity to put the spotlight on these deserving local heroes.


“When we heard about what these officers did, we knew they were true Hometown Heroes,” said Sondra Swensen, associate manager of Regional Brand Marketing at TDS. “They didn’t hesitate to step into a dangerous situation to help their neighbors get to safety. It was an honor for TDS to recognize their bravery and thank them for everything they do for the St. George community.”


For these nine officers, protecting their community is part of the job. But their courageous actions that day are a powerful example of what it means to step up when your neighbors need you most.
